For the last 12 years, I've been working on a project so close to my heart I made it the subject of doctoral dissertation at Florida State University. Until recently, I haven't had the time or focus to continue my work on what I've found to be a fascinating, challenging and spiritually-inquisitive subject: thousands of years of burying our dead, stories told through science, and how death shapes culture.
## Introducing "The People Buried Here"
Every major U.S. city was built atop an ancient one, and the hundreds of millions of people who lived and died here are still buried beneath it all. _**The People Buried Here**_ is an investigation of the burial places and practices of North America, over space and through time, and their marriage with modern physical and social infrastructure.
The story starts with Native American burial mounds plundered by road-pavers, earth movers and amateur archaeologists in South Louisiana, and advances to the Yellow Fever graveyards moved and resettled during 1960s suburban sprawl in the US Midwest.
This journalistically-styled series explores how and where people were buried, how those graves have been disturbed and destroyed, and how gravescapes cover nearly every corner of the places we live today.
_**The People Buried Here**_ strives to be a startling rediscovery of how we see the land we build our homes and businesses on, and the history of the very ground beneath us.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3710fdb0-52a9-407e-b320-243d4663eb64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ground-truthing mass graves identified via geospatial modeling with members of the Pointe-au-Chien Indian Tribe (PACIT).
We'll explore the science and history of burials and graves in America -- from the marshes in South Louisiana to Hart Island, New York. I discuss how climate change threatens some of our most ancient burial sites, and how scientists use technology to find those lost with time.
**This will be a subscriber-only project**. I've self-funded this project for more than a decade. Producing this series and launching this fall will be a full-time job. Each post and podcast episode includes interviews with researchers and experts and countless hours of research.
**You can subscribe now to get early and exclusive access to posts, podcasts and more.**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..RXVESK8uKfL706Wtt2q6Qup8trV2PurydETZeK-4q9c?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=146720491)
#### Here's what you can expect from the first 12 parts.
**Introduction:** The themes, history and science to be explored in the series. We'll go over how historians estimate the number of dead buried in America, how archaeologists have been at the forefront of finding historical gravesites using modern technology (including ground penetrating radar), and a brief summary of the episodes to come.
**South Louisiana and the cities built on bones** : The People Buried Here begins at a Native American mass burial site on the Pointe aux Chenes bayou in south Louisiana. This episode examines the burial places and practices of Native American tribes in the US South, and how those grave sites may and may not have been preserved based on location, soil type, environmental change. The chapter will highlight the standard burial places and rituals through time, and areas where the sites are disappearing into the rising waters below due to centuries of bayou fragmentation, oil and gas drilling, shipping, war, subsidence, hurricanes and climate change. Introduce the concept of camouflage and rebuilding on top of Native Cities.
**Caves, Catacombs and Crypts:** Not everyone is buried in the ground. In this episode, we look at other types of burial sites in America, including Native American burial caves in Appalachia, underground catacombs in Washington, DC and Indianapolis, St. Patrick's crypt in New York City, and the Old North Church crypt in Boston.
**American Vikings:** In Canada and northern Maine, researchers have been unearthing the lost history of Vikings in North America, reshaping what is known about their 500-year occupation of North America. At L'Anse aux Meadows, we speak with the research team about their discoveries and how ancient graves shed light on our understanding of world history.
**Yellow Fever:** Yellow Fever gravesites from Virginia to Mississippi and how the disease ravaged the early colonies and young America, killing 10% of the population in 1793. We'll visit historical sugar mills, which allowed the virus to spread, and how Yellow Fever resulted in sweeping regulations about the storage of food. We also tie-in how mosquito-borne illnesses are being introduced in the US South due to climate change, including Malaria, Dengue Fever and Zika, and how public health officials use past pandemics to inform responses to future ones.
**Antebellum** : In Altavista, Virginia, a plantation graveyard reveals how trafficking and imprisoned workers during slavery used hidden codes to mark the burial places of enslaved people. The same codes have been discovered at Avoca, VA, and other plantations across the south.
**Baltimore 's Son**: The bizarre story of one of the most famous graves in America: the final resting place of Edgar Allen Poe in Baltimore, Maryland. As strange and twisted as his writing, Poe's grave has its own remarkable history.
**Civil War:** Four battle sites, so overrun with bodies, were the resting place of soldiers killed in the civil war for decades. Bodies were buried where they fell, though many were dug up and reinterred elsewhere, many at Arlington National Cemetery. We investigate efforts to find bodies across these massive national parks, the history of reinterment of Civil War casualties, and touch on how a divided country practiced respect for the dead after the battle was done. Sites: Arlington, Antietam, Gettysburg, and Manassas.
**Poltergeist:** During the 1950's and 1960's, American suburbs expanded so quickly that cemeteries became victims of "progress." From Boone County, Kentucky to the Moses African Cemetery in Maryland, headstones were moved to make way for suburban sprawl, schools and even parking lots while the bodies were either moved or left behind.
We interview the people who exhume and reintern bodies when development impacts cemeteries and describe the process of "making room for the living by moving the dead." We explore how paranormal activity reflects our regard for graves as sacred spaces in American culture, and how it became the subject of a major motion picture riddled with its own tragic mysteries.
**Burial Playgrounds:** How cities and counties turned burial locations into parks to keep them from being destroyed, as well as modern efforts to locate lost graves, including GPR technology at the Tulsa Massacre site. We'll discuss efforts in places like Milton, Florida to preserve at-risk African American graveyards, and how unmarked graves are found and identified. This essay captures the dynamic history of burial practices in North America, showing how cultural, technological, and environmental factors have shaped the ways we honor our dead.
**Hart Island, New York** : An overview of Hart Island's use during the COVID-19 pandemic, including historical context from previous epidemics, namely HIV/AIDS. This chapter weaves together a narrative that spans centuries, focusing on Hart Island's evolving role in handling New York City's dead.
**Death Services** : Traditional and emerging ways Americans use death services. We cover the science of everything from embalming (where it started, why we do it, how it's done) and cremation to modern techniques like human composting and donation. Types of death services to be covered: Organ donation, donation to science, burial, direct burial, burial at sea, burial pods, cremation, hydro-cremation, cryofreezing, human composting, and other "green" burials.

After gauging the success of this series, I hope to expand the second part in 2025 to include:
**Underwater Cemeteries, Key West, Florida** : Hurricanes have a tendency to reveal secrets long lost in the past. In Florida, both at Cedar Key and Dry Tortugas, researchers have found underwater cemeteries with unmarked graves.
**Hawaii:** Royal Mausoleum at Mauna 'Ala, Hawaii and the preserved gravesite of the USS Arizona.
**Myles Standish Burial Ground, Massachusetts**
**Poverty Point, Mississippi: An ancient American empire**
**Ghost Dance: Wounded Knee Mass Grave**
**Mausoleums:** Mausoleums in America, with three famous Mausoleums as examples: Ulysses Grant, Woodlawn Cemetery in New York, and the famed St. Louis and Lafayette cemeteries of New Orleans.

You won't want to miss the culmination of more than a decade of work. Jul 17 | | | | | | | | | | | For the last 12 years, I've been working on a project so close to my heart I made it the subject of doctoral dissertation at Florida State University. Until recently, I haven't had the time or focus to continue my work on what I've found to be a fascinating, challenging and spiritually-inquisitive subject: thousands of years of burying our dead, stories told through science, and how death shapes culture. Introducing "The People Buried Here" Every major U.S. city was built atop an ancient one, and the hundreds of millions of people who lived and died here are still buried beneath it all. The People Buried Here is an investigation of the burial places and practices of North America, over space and through time, and their marriage with modern physical and social infrastructure. The story starts with Native American burial mounds plundered by road-pavers, earth movers and amateur archaeologists in South Louisiana, and advances to the Yellow Fever graveyards moved and resettled during 1960s suburban sprawl in the US Midwest. This journalistically-styled series explores how and where people were buried, how those graves have been disturbed and destroyed, and how gravescapes cover nearly every corner of the places we live today. The People Buried Here strives to be a startling rediscovery of how we see the land we build our homes and businesses on, and the history of the very ground beneath us. | | ---|---|--- Ground-truthing mass graves identified via geospatial modeling with members of the Pointe-au-Chien Indian Tribe (PACIT). We'll explore the science and history of burials and graves in America -- from the marshes in South Louisiana to Hart Island, New York. I discuss how climate change threatens some of our most ancient burial sites, and how scientists use technology to find those lost with time. This will be a subscriber-only project. I've self-funded this project for more than a decade. Producing this series and launching this fall will be a full-time job. Each post and podcast episode includes interviews with researchers and experts and countless hours of research. You can subscribe now to get early and exclusive access to posts, podcasts and more. Here's what you can expect from the first 12 parts. Introduction: The themes, history and science to be explored in the series. We'll go over how historians estimate the number of dead buried in America, how archaeologists have been at the forefront of finding historical gravesites using modern technology (including ground penetrating radar), and a brief summary of the episodes to come. South Louisiana and the cities built on bones : The People Buried Here begins at a Native American mass burial site on the Pointe aux Chenes bayou in south Louisiana. This episode examines the burial places and practices of Native American tribes in the US South, and how those grave sites may and may not have been preserved based on location, soil type, environmental change. The chapter will highlight the standard burial places and rituals through time, and areas where the sites are disappearing into the rising waters below due to centuries of bayou fragmentation, oil and gas drilling, shipping, war, subsidence, hurricanes and climate change. Introduce the concept of camouflage and rebuilding on top of Native Cities. Caves, Catacombs and Crypts: Not everyone is buried in the ground. In this episode, we look at other types of burial sites in America, including Native American burial caves in Appalachia, underground catacombs in Washington, DC and Indianapolis, St. Patrick's crypt in New York City, and the Old North Church crypt in Boston. American Vikings: In Canada and northern Maine, researchers have been unearthing the lost history of Vikings in North America, reshaping what is known about their 500-year occupation of North America. At L'Anse aux Meadows, we speak with the research team about their discoveries and how ancient graves shed light on our understanding of world history. Yellow Fever: Yellow Fever gravesites from Virginia to Mississippi and how the disease ravaged the early colonies and young America, killing 10% of the population in 1793. We'll visit historical sugar mills, which allowed the virus to spread, and how Yellow Fever resulted in sweeping regulations about the storage of food. We also tie-in how mosquito-borne illnesses are being introduced in the US South due to climate change, including Malaria, Dengue Fever and Zika, and how public health officials use past pandemics to inform responses to future ones. Antebellum : In Altavista, Virginia, a plantation graveyard reveals how trafficking and imprisoned workers during slavery used hidden codes to mark the burial places of enslaved people. The same codes have been discovered at Avoca, VA, and other plantations across the south. Baltimore 's Son: The bizarre story of one of the most famous graves in America: the final resting place of Edgar Allen Poe in Baltimore, Maryland. As strange and twisted as his writing, Poe's grave has its own remarkable history. Civil War: Four battle sites, so overrun with bodies, were the resting place of soldiers killed in the civil war for decades. Bodies were buried where they fell, though many were dug up and reinterred elsewhere, many at Arlington National Cemetery. We investigate efforts to find bodies across these massive national parks, the history of reinterment of Civil War casualties, and touch on how a divided country practiced respect for the dead after the battle was done. Sites: Arlington, Antietam, Gettysburg, and Manassas. Poltergeist: During the 1950's and 1960's, American suburbs expanded so quickly that cemeteries became victims of "progress." From Boone County, Kentucky to the Moses African Cemetery in Maryland, headstones were moved to make way for suburban sprawl, schools and even parking lots while the bodies were either moved or left behind. We interview the people who exhume and reintern bodies when development impacts cemeteries and describe the process of "making room for the living by moving the dead." We explore how paranormal activity reflects our regard for graves as sacred spaces in American culture, and how it became the subject of a major motion picture riddled with its own tragic mysteries. Burial Playgrounds: How cities and counties turned burial locations into parks to keep them from being destroyed, as well as modern efforts to locate lost graves, including GPR technology at the Tulsa Massacre site. We'll discuss efforts in places like Milton, Florida to preserve at-risk African American graveyards, and how unmarked graves are found and identified. This essay captures the dynamic history of burial practices in North America, showing how cultural, technological, and environmental factors have shaped the ways we honor our dead. Hart Island, New York : An overview of Hart Island's use during the COVID-19 pandemic, including historical context from previous epidemics, namely HIV/AIDS. This chapter weaves together a narrative that spans centuries, focusing on Hart Island's evolving role in handling New York City's dead. Death Services : Traditional and emerging ways Americans use death services. We cover the science of everything from embalming (where it started, why we do it, how it's done) and cremation to modern techniques like human composting and donation. Types of death services to be covered: Organ donation, donation to science, burial, direct burial, burial at sea, burial pods, cremation, hydro-cremation, cryofreezing, human composting, and other "green" burials. "The People Buried" here will be a subscriber-only publication and podcast. Subscribe today! After gauging the success of this series, I hope to expand the second part in 2025 to include: Underwater Cemeteries, Key West, Florida : Hurricanes have a tendency to reveal secrets long lost in the past. In Florida, both at Cedar Key and Dry Tortugas, researchers have found underwater cemeteries with unmarked graves. Hawaii: Royal Mausoleum at Mauna 'Ala, Hawaii and the preserved gravesite of the USS Arizona. Myles Standish Burial Ground, Massachusetts Poverty Point, Mississippi: An ancient American empire Ghost Dance: Wounded Knee Mass Grave Mausoleums: Mausoleums in America, with three famous Mausoleums as examples: Ulysses Grant, Woodlawn Cemetery in New York, and the famed St. Louis and Lafayette cemeteries of New Orleans. body:
| Peter, I know I’ve been sharing a lot of old photos recently, but I just had to send this to you.

Here you go. Me at 13, in all my “glory” at my Bar Mitzvah: [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/89043521/485996685/-972566244?amount=10&refcode=RTFC_20240717_EMSPL_E1_T0_AC&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwM2E5YTg5ZC02MzQ0LWVmMTEtODZjMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lI1k1P07q2BEs3dMMY38GSDzvKTdfXI1QsTdwHpAYaQ=) I’ll admit, it’s easy to chuckle at this photo — the classic 1970s bow tie, the braces, the yarmulke, the looks — but it is also an opportunity to tell you a little about how I approach my faith.

Throughout my career in public service, I’ve thought a lot about the Jewish tradition of “Tikkun Olam,” or repairing the world. And over the last few years, there has been a lot that was broken, and a lot to fix. It’s been my cause.

| | Today marks the 4-year anniversary of the passing of civil rights icon and House Democratic Sr. Chief Deputy Whip John Lewis. My late colleague is best known for his leadership in the civil rights movement and his brave actions to end legalized racial segregation in the United States, specifically leading the first march from Selma to Montgomery where state troopers and police attacked Congressman Lewis and the other marchers on the Edmund Pettus Bridge. **From the 1963 March on Washington, to sit-ins and the Freedom Rides, to the halls of Congress — Congressman Lewis was known for stirring up his trademark "good trouble" for the betterment of our society.** Folks have tried to capture the breadth and depth of his legacy through books and films, but the magnitude of his impact is beyond measure. The best I can hope to do is carry on a portion of that work in Congress. Like Congressman Lewis, I am committed to protecting the right to vote and defending our democratic institutions, values, and norms. I have proudly voted for landmark legislation to end partisan gerrymandering, require disclosure of dark money, expand opportunities to vote, and restore voting rights protections. **If we can reclaim a majority in Congress, I look forward to achieving these voting rights objectives by passing the legislation that bears his name: the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.** The Act would:
* Establish a formula that requires jurisdictions with a recent history of voter discrimination to seek approval from the U.S. Department of Justice before making changes to their voting laws
* Allow courts to immediately halt questionable voting practices pending a final ruling
* Provide the Attorney General the ability to request observers be present anywhere discriminatory voting practices pose a serious threat
* Increase transparency by requiring a public notice for changes to voting
* Help people seek justice for voting rights violations ahead of an election
* Create a grant funding program to help smaller jurisdictions comply with the legislation's new requirements

This legislation is more critical than ever. In the years since his passing, extremist Republicans have been hard at work eroding our basic democratic rights. **More often than not, their efforts seek to undermine the voices of people in traditionally marginalized communities**. Their unrelenting assaults on our democracy are disheartening, but after each blow, I have redoubled my commitment to ensuring every eligible voter's voice is heard. clean_body: CW: Racism, hate-based-violence | | | | Today marks the 4-year anniversary of the passing of civil rights icon and House Democratic Sr. Chief Deputy Whip John Lewis. My late colleague is best known for his leadership in the civil rights movement and his brave actions to end legalized racial segregation in the United States, specifically leading the first march from Selma to Montgomery where state troopers and police attacked Congressman Lewis and the other marchers on the Edmund Pettus Bridge. From the 1963 March on Washington, to sit-ins and the Freedom Rides, to the halls of Congress — Congressman Lewis was known for stirring up his trademark "good trouble" for the betterment of our society. Folks have tried to capture the breadth and depth of his legacy through books and films, but the magnitude of his impact is beyond measure. The best I can hope to do is carry on a portion of that work in Congress. Like Congressman Lewis, I am committed to protecting the right to vote and defending our democratic institutions, values, and norms. I have proudly voted for landmark legislation to end partisan gerrymandering, require disclosure of dark money, expand opportunities to vote, and restore voting rights protections. If we can reclaim a majority in Congress, I look forward to achieving these voting rights objectives by passing the legislation that bears his name: the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act. The Act would: Establish a formula that requires jurisdictions with a recent history of voter discrimination to seek approval from the U.S. Department of Justice before making changes to their voting laws Allow courts to immediately halt questionable voting practices pending a final ruling Provide the Attorney General the ability to request observers be present anywhere discriminatory voting practices pose a serious threat Increase transparency by requiring a public notice for changes to voting Help people seek justice for voting rights violations ahead of an election Create a grant funding program to help smaller jurisdictions comply with the legislation's new requirements This legislation is more critical than ever. In the years since his passing, extremist Republicans have been hard at work eroding our basic democratic rights. More often than not, their efforts seek to undermine the voices of people in traditionally marginalized communities. Their unrelenting assaults on our democracy are disheartening, but after each blow, I have redoubled my commitment to ensuring every eligible voter's voice is heard. Together, we can restore our democracy. To John Lewis, his memory, and all that he fought for. Friends,

When this campaign was just kicking off, I sent you all a survey asking about your priorities.

Most of you probably thought while filling out the survey that I wouldn’t actually sit down to read the results. But I did.

Your responses helped more than you know. I believe that candidates need to listen and learn to be effective leaders. Your responses told me what you care about most, what you want to change, and most of all, how I can be an effective representative for you in Congress.

You know my number one priority: representing Suffolk County values, not Trump values.

Now that the election season is heating up, I want to hear more from you. I want to listen to your ideas for the best path forward, and how my campaign can be even more effective in spreading the word and having these crucial conversations.

I know this: this is a campaign that is going to be won on kitchen table issues. Voters across Suffolk County are sick of getting bogged down in MAGA fights rather than working together to fix things like our broken immigration system and make our communities safer.

So please take this survey that my team and I put together and tell us what your priorities are. It’ll only take a few minutes to fill out, and it will help my campaign a lot. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/ibXtLhaOVkC_QjfoF99SUQ2]

I’ve always treated my campaign like a conversation, and this is no different. Productive conversations lead to problems being solved and lives improving. So, let’s keep the conversation going.

For veterans by helping pass legislation to expand VA benefits. For stronger Made-in-America rules to ensure our infrastructure is made with American iron and steel. For victims of the opioid crisis, pushing DC to help fight the epidemic. For affordable health care for all Wisconsinites. For the passage of the _Respect for Marriage Act_ , protecting marriage equality for all. There’s not enough room in this email, or a hundred emails, to list all of Tammy Baldwin’s accomplishments. But despite her years of service to Wisconsin, **the polls are tightening. body:
We wanted to take a minute to share a little bit about another young progressive candidate who should be on your radar.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20240717&t=1&akid=952%2E587540%2EdwaoxS)
Hey Peter,
We wanted to take a minute to share a little bit about another young progressive candidate who should be on your radar. Her name is **Kristian Carranza** , and she’s running for the Texas State House of Representatives!
**[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240717?refcode=em20240717&amount=5&refcode2=952_587540_dwaoxS&akid=952%2E587540%2EdwaoxS)**
Kristian lives on the Southside of **San Antonio** and she’s exactly the kind of leader we need in office. She grew up with a single mom who worked hard to provide for her family, and she’s been working to help provide for herself and her family since she was 16 years old. Since then, she’s registered over 10,000 voters in Texas and is now ready to bring the fight to the Texas State House.
And with Greg Abbott expected to introduce a slew of **harmful, backward bills** in the legislature next year, Kristian’s victory could be crucial in preventing some of them from passing.
**[If you want to help Kristian win, will you split a donation of $5 or more between her campaign and Leaders We Deserve today?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240717?refcode=em20240717&amount=5&refcode2=952_587540_dwaoxS&akid=952%2E587540%2EdwaoxS)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240717?amount=5&refcode=em20240717-952&refcode2=952_587540_dwaoxS&akid=952%2E587540%2EdwaoxS)**
Here are just a few of the things we’re expecting to see in the legislature next year:
* **More school voucher bills** that would defund public schools and send that money to private religious schools instead
* **More NRA-backed bills** that increase the risk of gun violence
* **More attacks on LGBTQ+ people**
* **More limits on access to abortion** and other reproductive health services

But Peter, here’s the good news: _Kristian’s race is competitive._ In fact, she’s running in the only state house district in Texas that’s held by a Republican and that **both Biden and Beto O’Rourke won.**
By flipping this seat blue, Kristian can increase our chances of stopping Abbott’s backward policies from becoming law and she can help shine a spotlight on the issues young people care about most.
**Competitive races are always expensive though, and you can bet Texas Republicans will spend big to hang on to this seat.**

Making dinner and taking calls before my evening events — that's just the reality of being a working mom, friend!
As my campaign starts cooking with gas (pun fully intended 😉), I find myself taking solace in the normal moments at home. Don't get me wrong, I love being on the campaign trail, too: Talking to voters, traveling around Florida, running a battleground Senate race — I don't take a second of it for granted.

But here's what I also don't take for granted, friend: dinners at home with my three kids and husband, Sundays playing dominoes with my mom, and conversations with my children about what's been going on at school.
I love being a parent. But parents all over our nation — perhaps you, too, friend — share the same sinking feeling right now: Our kids are growing up in a country with fewer freedoms than we had at their age.

_I'm in this race to protect, restore, and defend our freedoms. To preserve our democracy. _

My opponent, Sen. Rick Scott, is directly responsible for confirming Supreme Court justices who have eviscerated reproductive rights and weakened voting rights. **_Ya no más — enough is enough._**
This is our greatest opportunity to defeat extremist Rick Scott and protect our democracy. | | | | | Peter — Tonight, we close the books on the last official FEC fundraising deadline before we know who our opponent will be in the November election. This isn't one of those quarterly FEC deadlines we email about, but it is an official deadline — and probably the most important of the campaign. Here's why: After July 17th, we're legally required to report what we've raised and how much money we have in the bank since our last deadline on June 30th. Same for our eventual opponent. Our report will give super PACs a glimpse at the financial strength of our campaign just before we formally enter the general election, and they will use that information when deciding whether or not to run attack ads against us, or if they should move on to another race. We want to file as strong a report as we possibly can, but with only 17 days between deadlines, that’s going to require a lot of support from a whole bunch of people giving whatever they can. I wish we didn't have to make these requests this often via email, but the truth is it is where a majority of the donations we receive come from. So, I am asking: [**Can I count on you to contribute $10 to my campaign for U.S. Senate in Michigan and Blue Amp Action before the final FEC fundraising deadline of the primary campaign comes to a close tonight?**](https://default.salsalabs.org/Ta39be099-65cb-4ee2-985a-319a2f44fa1e/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

Over the past decade it has infected democratic societies--including ours. It is as simple as it is terrifying: What we do now will define the future of our country and world. We at Blue Amp Action are dedicated to liberal, open societies, where reason and science are applied to solve our problems; where civil rights--including voting rights!--are protected for all. We fight for these values every day. Speaking up on our platforms, raising the voices and the political prospects of liberal pols and pundits. **And savvy grassroots activists like you know, just like we do, that we can’t stop watching the people we help elect:_ after the elections, we have to keep organizing support for the policies we like and pushing back against the ones we don’t._** **__When the public tunes out between elections and the only people our elected officials hear from are the paid lobbyists of wealthy corporations, our government stops being accountable to the needs of ordinary families.__** **Democracy never sleeps, and neither can we.** So we ask that you support our work, so we can continue to engage in this fight every moment of every day. Friend, I’m not telling you this only in hopes that you’ll rush for your pocket book. I’m telling you this because I want you to know what type of man my husband is. This is Amy Brown and my husband Sam Brown is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Nevada. I first met my husband in the burn unit when he returned from Afghanistan after a roadside bomb exploded under his vehicle. There was one thing about Sam that caught my attention immediately. It wasn’t the burns on his body, it wasn’t the scars on the face. His vibrant faith in God glowed brightly even in his darkest days. Everyone that encountered Sam could see it. For me, Sam was a light that guided me, challenged me, and reconnected me with God and the Church. I had grown up in the Church but had lost my Faith – I was at my rock bottom until I met Sam. During that time, I shared with him some of the struggles I had faced. He told me he was concerned for my Salvation – and for that matter so was I. **[That brought us to where we are today, 15 years later. We have 3 kids and I’m a Bible-believing momma who puts Bible lessons in our family's homeschool curriculum.](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=c141e36c6fb8476c85759a46850d0886&_e=Ik-AfzlfbQvB1It4s9aepGhb5xrtLhLsAIvVhqznKSmkbd57PQ-f6OoXKqqHGiq97rHFgsbwxhAI4kBqItBlLAuQRrtdPcc8aGI_TFX6NmGwqQuQ46eAEduB7Fzcou3IkhTqN9d4LUbJkaukO5yv8EFAK6N3n4DSvwiAWt36wfa3p5dMYQCCsAaDWlzYM-1v2i6jj-nqSAENjXu86bEoU82V9-39o2JDeaIrGOUi-E2hgJf-UIPbebiX1SHYuluKq1G5_12lKfk11VDmyQlVcPZSq3wrTDj4iK-2a70OV9P7vHfiOX9AP9zLCyilIMCoRqiKd6_Zu56S4Nz3pX5hEv9MHGENabmsRSj-m3YGNHXCclnxl7FkS5tigSMOdKEJEn1yzIqkTMr4aWaauqmZw0g1Z40f21UtA76SsUi3ExC8fCBKpZvVJZx9V9tzCIyaYm1NGIfDu_WgPWeUY9ucaw%3D%3D)** Friend, if i hadn't gone through my darkest days, I may have never met Sam and never found a way back to God the way that I did. **[Everything Sam had planned to do with his life changed in 60 seconds in Afghanistan, but it never changed who he was.](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=c141e36c6fb8476c85759a46850d0886&_e=Ik-AfzlfbQvB1It4s9aepGhb5xrtLhLsAIvVhqznKSmkbd57PQ-f6OoXKqqHGiq97rHFgsbwxhAI4kBqItBlLAuQRrtdPcc8aGI_TFX6NmGwqQuQ46eAEduB7Fzcou3IkhTqN9d4LUbJkaukO5yv8EFAK6N3n4DSvwiAWt36wfa3p5dMYQCCsAaDWlzYM-1v2i6jj-nqSAENjXu86bEoU82V9-39o2JDeaIrGOUi-E2hgJf-UIPbebiX1SHYuluKq1G5_12lKfk11VDmyQlVcPZSq3wrTDj4iK-2a70OV9P7vHfiOX9AP9zLCyilIMCorYqYWNFUOJSkdK_9lZ9Yie5RtmTwwhjJjPD1KqH355kOjGE0JSZSCX9x7faxL0Z1T0GoWF515rmVfa3CV1bqpFlOh9W5kj091YUSPCk_fuSQLbQCsMxXDTryDn5xt-TmuiQZdPkFG6dY7XB42R0B5w%3D%3D) ** His faith never wavered. His hope never left him. His dedication and desire to serve has not faded to this day. Although he would never be permitted to return to the line of duty on account of his injuries, he never stopped fighting for others. I'll be honest with you. This campaign hasn’t been easy on our family. _**[_**Today I wanted to ask you to help Sam and our whole family make this sacrifice worthwhile.**_](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=c141e36c6fb8476c85759a46850d0886&_e=Ik-AfzlfbQvB1It4s9aepGhb5xrtLhLsAIvVhqznKSmkbd57PQ-f6OoXKqqHGiq97rHFgsbwxhAI4kBqItBlLAuQRrtdPcc8aGI_TFX6NmGwqQuQ46eAEduB7Fzcou3IkhTqN9d4LUbJkaukO5yv8EFAK6N3n4DSvwiAWt36wfa3p5dMYQCCsAaDWlzYM-1v2i6jj-nqSAENjXu86bEoU82V9-39o2JDeaIrGOUi-E2hgJf-UIPbebiX1SHYuluKq1G5_12lKfk11VDmyQlVcPZSq3wrTDj4iK-2a70OV9P7vHfiOX9AP9zLCyilIMCo76MFErPnrnMuXjWzzWwuSrL7wYmBhrUYcobpkLvEhXjuuGMNXbglJGAEk-UUG5odXKNygIR-EhGg-e6AMV652qL0UGQEs6aItskWOxZlFEasrnyr4jlm-wwrA7yLFx_KXL7yMxMl1QQJQrT4vl5PCQ%3D%3D)**_ ** _**[Would you please consider making a donation of any amount to Sam’s I want to share a personal message with you Friend.

**After graduating high school, I enlisted in the military and served our country for more than 12 years.** I served under the elite Joint Special Operations Command (JSOC) as a bomb disposal expert, which was dangerous and often deadly work.

---
| [](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=64877a52c2534d66a75ede7619cd99bd&_e=CCs07DRR0ypGXbdHONO7TfPmXkKvAppQG4XV2SW49Ji6aMoxuGYaZxiiMyYjkin0WsnQqN6VDjZU-PW38Z7GJ_6Zs4HDyf6boV_NITXBl6ReNg9CIaWssE1Pg4RExC9kWd24fg2JN820llBQzowZSlKC1DICyX1qy1TeHW5D2kSWxFPqKZpg9eMRue6HB6aAShOQvud0_VzcAd12yy9Wk5eaArRNaVxFVMyLOFIgOO0KvewiTwfPvUUVsvUpHo73ld7rDa4vXxiK4HcWAUKKbT8mE-htzc20q698LyUlt0gYcHzwzobzxf5Q6nV9Yz9d-sJ_ui2T29nOPdJ5_8G4KoboyfhpZO0AxfCg-GoqSdtOR4HUyFuep5hznNprJB9nJc-DHFv8teUL4W1llqzeBn248EpqsGvWoE6IfUTHz18%3D)

**While I was able to detect and destroy most of these IEDs, the very last IED resulted in sustained catastrophic injuries, including the loss of both my legs.

When I awoke after injury in Walter Reed Army Medical Center,** my focus was singular: get better, get back to work and get back to serving America.

subject: Women for Mackenzie

body:
VOTE RYAN MACKENZIE FOR U.S. CONGRESS | | | | |
---
|
---
| Friends,
As a state Representative, I have always fought for everyday Pennsylvanians. In Congress, my commitment will remain the same. We need to save the middle class, protect seniors, give new hope to young people, and fight for working families.
This week, I want to highlight some of the accomplishments I’ve made as a state Representative to help the women and families of Pennsylvania. In Congress, I will be able to do even more!
* I authored a law establishing Pennsylvania’s Maternal Mortality Heath Review Committee that is helping to reduce maternal mortality across our state. [(ACT 24 2018)](https://mackenzieforcongress.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=62252a4538e3fe848298033c5&id=ab28726b5e&e=5ccada9200)

* I authored a bill that passed the House to help domestic violence victims by amending the Unemployment Compensation (UC) Law to make it easier for them to receive benefits if they are forced to quit their job because continued employment would jeopardize their safety.

* I introduced a [Pennsylvania Families Tax Relief Package](https://mackenzieforcongress.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=62252a4538e3fe848298033c5&id=858eb96980&e=5ccada9200) to help reduce costs for working families, and everyone. An expansion of Pennsylvania’s Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit was included in last year’s budget.

* I sponsored a bill to combat sexual exploitation using new computer technology. My legislation forbids the use of “deepfake” technology that uses someone’s image to create pornographic content without their permission.

* I passed a resolution designating Maternal Health Day in Pennsylvania to bring much-needed attention to the risks and challenges faced by many expecting mothers.

* I’m a member of the PA Black Maternal Mortality Caucus, which seeks to address the disproportionately high mortality rate for Black mothers.

This record - and my commitment to continuing to advance issues like this in Congress - is why I am proud to launch our “Women for Mackenzie” coalition with the help of great women from across the 7th District.
**WOMEN FOR MACKENZIE WILL BE HEADED BY:**

* Chaired by: Rochelle Pasquariello (Carbon County)
* Co-Chair: Susan Cowell (Northampton County)
* Co-Chair: Monica Chibber (Lehigh County)
* Co-Chair: Ann Gravell (Monore County)

As always, if you need to contact the campaign, please feel free to reach out at (484) 347-8777.

---
| Thank you,
Team Mackenzie

Last week’s flooding occurred on the same date as our July 2023 floods, and it’s not lost on me how much natural disasters have put the people of Vermont through. I am deeply troubled by the impact of climate change on Vermont’s infrastructure, businesses, economy, but most of all, on its people. I will continue to do everything I can to fight for my Mental Health Emergency Needs in Disasters (MEND) Act in Congress, so that mental health care is prioritized in federal disaster recovery programs and Vermonters have access to this care when they need it most. And, as always, bold action to combat climate change remains on the forefront of my priorities. We are still assessing the damage that’s been done, but I know Vermonters have already been helping their neighbors clean up and recover. I want to encourage you to visit **[Vermont211.org](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/89051697/486024606/-1385185222?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhOTk3MzFlMi03NjQ0LWVmMTEtODZjMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LFDP9FOROKH1GTUEsV-zsdDsoNukVxBWV7s6SiZAxXw=&emci=2681f95f-6944-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&emdi=a99731e2-7644-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&ceid=43402272)** to report any damage you have experienced as a result of last week’s flooding — even if you are not in need of assistance, your report helps us increase our assessments and qualify for more federal assistance for Vermonters in need! In moments like these, I’m reminded of the grit and resilience of Vermonters. I’ve seen neighbors step up to lend a hand, and I’ve seen communities support local businesses as they reopen and recover. I know that we will always rise to the occasion and come back stronger than ever — it’s simply who we are in the Green Mountain State. My thoughts are with you,
Becca Balint

I want to share a personal message with you Friend.

**After graduating high school, I enlisted in the military and served our country for more than 12 years.** I served under the elite Joint Special Operations Command (JSOC) as a bomb disposal expert, which was dangerous and often deadly work.

---
| [](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=97ff1987166d42a0854b0766c0c319ff&_e=uiCDG0D2wA5mYvl8JC1mW1ovA0usj7os1oZLYxsW7nt8jsgequDzd0fvuiKhIKEMJPvg59t-Xpd63XN3yC4MM3M_TNKimUoI4URh8ltLqKHjjqminEco21SS9KAIezcl0GyfmVTIGKOU75-Bjbl3x1VNJ6O8MsLxgJp7FIJK_hffyuoouGJlofjGoaqNkuwf9lcuj_qYRo53-7RH0jAlDOOzz8dKszjc9yQy8tJd84NpoVE68remPjqHCmeS6AB5A1hSlNd-a5sCHXCZYj2WDjbQHzFGs85tIQXA_2TNChJ7Dy0DJZiQufiHhHY2iBzTSNcV8myNBUIR3xfANp7-N_OF0H5qRqSf9S4UE5f9FoLNuvP4NLVMzfjlEkOM3FpWmxDP0cjsIf8Y8_P_I4Ir2A%3D%3D)
---

**While I was able to detect and destroy most of these IEDs, the very last IED resulted in sustained catastrophic injuries, including the loss of both my legs.

When I awoke after injury in Walter Reed Army Medical Center,** my focus was singular: get better, get back to work and get back to serving America.

---
| [](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=97ff1987166d42a0854b0766c0c319ff&_e=uiCDG0D2wA5mYvl8JC1mW1ovA0usj7os1oZLYxsW7nt8jsgequDzd0fvuiKhIKEMJPvg59t-Xpd63XN3yC4MM3M_TNKimUoI4URh8ltLqKHjjqminEco21SS9KAIezcl0GyfmVTIGKOU75-Bjbl3x1VNJ6O8MsLxgJp7FIJK_hffyuoouGJlofjGoaqNkuwf9lcuj_qYRo53-7RH0jAlDOOzz8dKszjc9yQy8tJd84NpoVE68remPjqHCmeS6AB50CUUYTnLph_BSQiDjKN6Q9ywFJS3iZwiv1LB7IcEXw9bWIWMubpnIrXq968TR8c_8PGWk0zLgCxmNgZcl-7Xm8fHISw5E68QSAGbug4wu2zU6UO933OPrg6I-_-hNXx0pmmSLzZlUOA2VFk_vaOcfA%3D%3D)

**Once I retired from the military, I knew there was still work left to do, so I ran for Congress and was elected by the people of Florida to bring a Conservative voice to Washington.**

body:
In a few hours, JD Vance will address the Republican National Convention in Milwaukee as Donald Trump’s running mate for the first time. Before he takes the stage, I felt compelled to remind you exactly who Vance is.
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/89053962/486032900/149134340?refcode=header&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDc0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NmQxMTY2MC03YjQ0LWVmMTEtODZjMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=plkQfNFkPTe6iqEIi5pgX47UAPHrL7TcN-P27jLbUEE=)
---
Peter,
In a few hours, JD Vance will address the Republican National Convention in Milwaukee as Donald Trump’s running mate for the first time. Before he takes the stage, I felt compelled to remind you exactly who Vance is.
I grew up in a small town, and let me tell you: JD Vance doesn’t know what makes small-towns in America tick.
Small towns don’t work because everyone is closed-minded and prejudiced. Small towns work because people mind their own damn business. You respect your neighbor and their choices. You respect who they love. You respect their health care decisions and what books they read.
**JD Vance has a real problem with minding his own damn business,** **Peter.** He voted against IVF access and wants to criminalize abortion rights nationally without exceptions for rape and incest survivors.
Vance rails against the Affordable Care Act, which provides protections for millions of Americans with pre-existing conditions, and has attacked Social Security and Medicare as “the biggest roadblocks to any kind of real fiscal sanity.”
JD Vance is a cynical fraud. He’s the Heritage Foundation’s perfect Frankenstein monster, and if he and Trump are elected in November, they’ll stop at nothing to advance their extreme Project 2025 agenda from the White House.

Today, we close the books on the last official FEC fundraising deadline before we know who our opponent will be in the November election.
This isn't one of those quarterly FEC deadlines we email about, but it is an official deadline — and probably the most important of the campaign.
Here's why:
After today, we're legally required to report what we've raised and how much money we have in the bank since our last deadline on June 30th. Same for our eventual opponent.
Our report will give super PACs a glimpse at the financial strength of our campaign just before we formally enter the general election, and they will use that information when deciding whether or not to run attack ads against us, or if they should move on to another race.
We want to file as strong a report as we possibly can, but with only 17 days between deadlines, that’s going to require a lot of support from a whole bunch of people giving whatever they can.
I wish we didn't have to make these requests this often via email, but the truth is it is where a majority of the donations we receive come from. So, I am asking:
Can I count on you to contribute $10 to my campaign for U.S. Senate in Michigan and Tim Kaine before the final FEC fundraising deadline of the primary campaign comes to a close in just a few hours? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-slotkin]

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: My Decision
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BOB CASEY FOR SENATE INC
body:
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20240717-3?refcode=em20240717-3&refcode2=3582_552475_0iNrRr&akid=3582%2E552475%2E0iNrRr)
Peter —
While I know our campaign has sent a lot of emails before tonight's FEC deadline (yes, a very real one before Michigan's primary), I want to take a few minutes to tell you about my decision to run for Senate in the first place, and why your support is so important in our success.
The truth is, we all know America is going through something right now. We seem to be living from crisis to crisis. But there are certain things that should be really simple:
Like living a middle-class life in the state that invented the middle class.
Like making things in America so that we’re in control of our own economic security.
Like protecting our children from the things that are truly harming them.
And preserving our rights and our democracy so that our kids can live their version of the American dream.
I’m running for Senate because I believe that we need a new generation of leaders that thinks differently, works harder, and never forgets that we are public servants.
But my decision to run for Senate is also deeply personal to me, and it's related to what motivated me to first run for the House in 2018.
It's about my mom. She was diagnosed with stage IV ovarian cancer in 2009 — and didn't have health insurance at the time. She had let it lapse after the insurance companies had gouged her for years because she happened to have a pre-existing condition. She passed away in 2011, but that experience — of desperately trying to get her care at the same moment we were filling out bankruptcy paperwork — motivated me to run then, and keeps me motivated to fight now. I remember the exact moment that I decided to enter public office: when the then-GOP controlled House of Representatives, the body I now serve in, voted to repeal those protections for people with pre-existing conditions.
Six years later, the Republican leaders, fueled by the extreme wing of the party, are continuing the march to repeal things that the average Americans want. They want to privatize Social Security and Medicare, repeal drug price protections like allowing Medicare to negotiate, then there’s the rights they’re obsessed with repealing: a woman’s right to choose, voting rights, and any possible gun safety legislation.
By winning this Senate seat, we’ll help ensure that Democrats retain the (slight!) majority and can pass legislation that expands access to healthcare. Not the obsession with taking things away.
To be upfront: **Winning this race is going to take a lot of resources. A crazy amount. And we have to do it without raising a single dollar from corporate PACs.**
Donations this November — when we’re in the home stretch — are important. But donations now are even more important, because they allow us to map out a strategic plan and make decisions about when and how we reach voters.
**[That is why I would love it if you would consider donating $10 or whatever you can to Bob Casey and my campaigns before our FEC fundraising deadline ends tonight at midnight.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20240717-3?refcode=em20240717-3&refcode2=3582_552475_0iNrRr&akid=3582%2E552475%2E0iNrRr)**
**[Donate Now ››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20240717-3?refcode=em20240717-3&refcode2=3582_552475_0iNrRr&akid=3582%2E552475%2E0iNrRr)**
Thank you,
Elissa

The Latino Vote Episode 48 - Featuring Antonia Cereijido

Our guest, **award-winning journalist Antonia Cereijido** , shares insights from her podcast, "**[Imperfect Paradise: Return to Mexico](https://vote.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2e84c756a73b2b9193783ffd1&id=5680f8a478&e=5bd167f239).**" This four part series examines the real-life consequences of U.S. immigration and the porous reality of those with lives on both sides of the border.

'Return to Mexico explores **what happens to returnees after deportation** through the lens of Daniel Zamora.' [Click here to access the four-part series.](https://vote.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2e84c756a73b2b9193783ffd1&id=3a7c89ff20&e=5bd167f239)

| | **Our work in Wisconsin paid off – we're proud to report another victory for voting rights in this important battleground state!** Just two years ago, the far-right majority on the Wisconsin Supreme Court issued a near-total ban on absentee ballot drop boxes, eliminating a safe, easy, and convenient way to vote and get back to your day. Then came last year's special election to replace a retiring Supreme Court judge – a race we knew could change the entire balance of the Court. So, we jumped in this race to target and push less-frequent voters to cast their ballots in an election that got nowhere near the same level of attention as, say, the presidency. We used technology that sends the location and image of the voter's polling place straight to them via text message. Our research shows that receiving this kind of message helps potential vote-skippers visualize the act of voting (and how easy it is to do) and increases their propensity to vote by another percentage point. And it was a success! **Cut to earlier this month when the new liberal majority on the Court said what everyone knows to be true. Ballot drop boxes are safe, convenient, easy, and just make sense. And now, in a state where Joe Biden won in 2020 by less than 1%, Wisconsin voters have the right to cast their ballots quickly and easily!** This is the kind of work that has huge impacts down the line. We're thrilled to see this expansion of voters' rights in Wisconsin! Thanks for your support, _Sarah_ Sarah Long
Director of Development

So, we jumped in this race to target and push less-frequent voters to cast their ballots in an election that got nowhere near the same level of attention as, say, the presidency. We used technology that sends the location and image of the voter's polling place straight to them via text message. Our research shows that receiving this kind of message helps potential vote-skippers visualize the act of voting (and how easy it is to do) and increases their propensity to vote by another percentage point. And it was a success! Cut to earlier this month when the new liberal majority on the Court said what everyone knows to be true. Ballot drop boxes are safe, convenient, easy, and just make sense. And now, in a state where Joe Biden won in 2020 by less than 1%, Wisconsin voters have the right to cast their ballots quickly and easily! This is the kind of work that has huge impacts down the line. We're thrilled to see this expansion of voters' rights in Wisconsin! My name is Hung Cao, and America saved my life. From a young age, I knew I wanted to pay back this country for all it had done for me. Our border is wide open, and American families have paid the price with violent crime and even the lives of their loved ones. Look, I’m an immigrant myself, but my family and I came here the right way, and we obeyed American laws and embraced the American culture. _That’s not what’s happening today. _ I love this country so much that I wrote a blank check up to and including my life for it. **[I’m not going to let Joe Biden and the radical Left take away what I and so many other brave men and women fought for.](http://links.hungcaoforva.com/u/click?_t=c514f30bd6cd4b1bb0e09a0456675c53&_m=9a2a17d177604aa7a8c4b05035af3cda&_e=uZXSkF3jBHYfhS0V_tlytl-O9SbkHG6W1awRVjSnspidd1rXI1qpRhVh53aHdrUHoM4QC5DoUaLstZD6eqf4tggGcty0LmC3mVZDJRgASjSNODZRpeWht5W0hIFYSmnfqsFiLbZLmSfTLxxWfhDBZL5qAmDu_sm3s0Ed0QKCmQ-Pf4oklzgUT0XCpd3NR-RverBtorpo-DilH33uEcNSaIZFt1N-4Dz_PYv7X3HcHDlWNJxsLZXbQOjBpRUcTLepKPTnrUNEDrpulOMnV8oi-RJv2wbhJPU6Khq-3FC4BsbJUl57_FJsubDoisin-0yS2bvZAHFZ4YZQrJ0Z1fcHafUWHIo6AwM4MxaCfwZXpsE%3D)**

subject: From All 50 States: nearly $1 million raised to unseat Jim Jordan
body:
https://www.tamiewilson.com/ [https://www.tamiewilson.com/]
Friends,
Exciting news!
I’m thrilled to announce that our campaign has hit some major milestones:
First, we are quickly closing in on raising one million dollars in our fight to unseat do-nothing Congressman Jim Jordan.
This impressive figure is helped by the fact that last fundraising quarter, we received donations from all 50 states!
It's amazing to see that folks all across the country want in on our fight, they believe in our mission, and know we have what it takes to defeat one of the most ULTRA-MAGA congressmen out there.
And get this—we’ve had nearly 43,000 donations, with the average donation being $19.46.
That’s right—we’re closing in on one million dollars, mainly raised from grassroots donations that average under $20.
We are showing the country that we are one of the strongest community-backed grassroots movements in the nation! Everyone knows my race is the most important Congressional race in the country because I am running to unseat the most unethical, immoral, dangerous man in Congress.
Voters are tired of the constant MAGA gridlock and are ready for leaders who will prioritize the needs of working families, veterans, and our communities. Our campaign is about more than just winning an election; it's about delivering real results. Join our fight. Help us continue to build our resources and contribute today! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20240717_fundraising_numbers_link1]
Your support has been instrumental in getting us this far, and it’s clear that our message is resonating not just in our district but across the entire country.
This fundraising quarter alone, we raised over $250,000, and it's clear why:
Jim Jordan is an extremist do-nothing who has consistently voted against veterans, women, farmers, and the working class 97% of the time. SHAMEFUL! It doesn't get any more anti-American than that, does it?
Despite being in Congress since 2007, Jordan has never authored and passed a bill into law, he’s too extreme.
That means he’s been paid 3 million dollars to betray America and accomplish zero for our district.
Would you still have a job and collect a paycheck if you didn’t get anything done for 17 years?
I don’t think so.
Let’s keep this energy going! Your support has gotten us this far, and with your continued help we can outpace and outperform Jim Jordan and his ULTRA-MAGA agenda. Let’s finish what we’ve started and make history. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20240717_fundraising_numbers_link2]
Working for US,
Tamie Wilson

Since Donald Trump launched his political career on the racist birtherism attacks on President Obama, racism and white supremacy have defined the MAGA movement. That racism has had violent consequences. Who can forget Trump's[ vile and violent tweets targeting Asian Americans, and the resulting massive spikes in hate crimes](https://substack.com/redirect/b305e974-83f2-4a36-8dda-dc450303b134?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)? Perhaps this is why JD Vance himself condemned Donald Trump when he said in a now deleted tweet, "_Trump makes people I care about afraid. Immigrants, Muslims, etc. Because of this I find him reprehensible. God wants better of us_ "
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/24cf36f2-eed5-4a5d-b84f-44feea7b3457?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

JD Vance's now deleted tweet condemning Donald Trump's racism and Islamophobia
I guess God _doesn 't _want better of us, according to JD Vance? Now as the "American Hitler"--as Vance likes to call Trump--taps Vance to be his VP, Vance's wife Usha Chilukuri Vance comes into the spotlight as the potential future Second Lady. Usha is a Yale Law graduate. She clerked for Justice Roberts, then Justice Kavanaugh, and is now an accomplished corporate lawyer. She even, as the NY Times put it, "_helped Mr. Vance organize his ideas about social decline in rural white America_." By all accounts she's been vital to advancing not only JD Vance's racism and claims of white grievance, but intimately supported a rogue MAGA Supreme Court rife with corruption to advance Project 2025. Usha should be a MAGA hero for advancing the MAGA agenda of racism and white supremacy.
There's only one problem for the MAGA crowd--she's not white. Usha is an Indian American and daughter of Indian immigrants. And the grotesque racism and white supremacy that has defined the MAGA movement, is now coming for her.
**Let 's Address This.**

Ohio Sen. JD Vance and his wife, Usha Vance at the RNC in Milwaukee on July 15, 2024. Credit: Anna Moneymaker/Getty
No sooner did Donald Trump tap JD Vance to be his VP but the MAGA racist outrage machine went into overdrive--led by none other than avowed white supremacist Nick Fuentes. Fuentes, you'll recall, is the white supremacist, antisemitic, Islamophobic, xenophobic extremist who visited Mar-a-Lago and had dinner with Donald Trump. Trump never disavowed him, nor has the GOP. Fuentes now [complains about JD Vance](https://substack.com/redirect/59a0aca5-1ffc-4813-b9d0-cc741adc4a0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),
> Who is this guy, really? Do we really expect that the guy who has an Indian wife and named their kid Vivek is going to support white identity?
Even prior to accepting a spot on the ballot for VP, the MAGA crowd condemned Vance for daring to have "mixed race children with Indian names." See Exhibit A
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a8ebfc8e-3705-4b1b-8fc6-f5ef3e87e41a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

And MAGA white supremacists have not been subtle about their hatred of Usha Vance either, specifically because she is Indian American and the daughter of immigrants. See Exhibit B, Exhibit C, and Exhibit D.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/833a0e9f-5b8a-4ab4-8b79-16cff0ae8d66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

---|---|---

And these are but snapshots of an avalanche of hate directed at Usha Vance because she is not white. Frankly, I find it helpful that MAGAs are now openly acknowledging that the Republican plan is to "destroy" anyone nonwhite, because at least now we can drop the pretense that their policies are based on some sort of noble values, but instead recognize that they are in fact based in overt fascism. It's no surprise therefore, that other MAGAs are trying to 'make eugenics great again,' claiming that maybe Usha is acceptable because she has "more European physiognomy." See Exhibit E.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2c8720ef-8210-4b08-81aa-6f152b19f52e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

And to be sure, Usha Vance isn't the only Indian woman berated for the 'crime' of being Indian. Sikh American Harmeet Dhillon is a known loyal GOP operative with bonafide MAGA credentials. Dear friend,
I want to take a minute to personally thank each of you for your support in my campaign.
More than ever we need to come together and pray for our country. I am deeply grateful President Trump is in good health following the horrific assassination attempt this past weekend. My prayers are with the family of Corey Comperatore, the brave patriot who tragically lost his life at the rally. All Americans, no matter their politics must condemn political violence.

When I write these weekly emails, it reminds me of the reason I am running for Congress...to make our country safer for you and our families. It’s why I get up everyday and fight the good fight. And I will never quit.

|

The countdown to Election Day is on, and we're fired up and ready to win! **** **Only 33 days to go until the primary election on August 20th!**

subject: Secret Service Director, Kimberly Cheatle, Needs to Resign
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Banks for Senate
body:
Sign the Petition

|
---
Fellow American,

The events of July 13, 2024, in Butler, PA, when President Trump was almost assassinated, should have never taken place if the Secret Service had completely secured the perimeter of the rally.

We now know that not only did the Secret Service leave a rooftop with a clear view of President Trump unguarded, but they were aware of the threat for 10 minutes before President Trump took the stage, and still allowed the event to proceed.

A one-on-one matchup with Adam Schiff on November 5th. **[**Can I count on your contribution of $6 to help defeat Adam Schiff today?**](http://links.rightwaypress.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=e00b9716d4f743d781146f101d6bf1fd&_e=suePF1CEXmlXo39hoovKcNP1x0G5Tr3iWeiWiIiEo9bN11EJOltxGc9adIK4AsLPBfkySgA5D-xwWsS5b2Mf_tvKiMbJYRbIOYYvdEgovfWCakWMMZkiIkaH9Mjme-z1O2_bET9cix8l8ebKp_rnz3KhibJULz634Jd4eZdKRiYjlKt2W2R9uUNX2mInE_JekJV05YlSXNPKUHqzieTkUHy9CS59XXndtX5ShtCJz-ScVRGiFrxNbSqgJkA7uJelxMP0J7EqgvpCFlV-7CZtVfxWgXzzWVdzU7Kfunx1zv4B-s0URVpZmt7u6TPums6ObWZNjq_wD5NNnQPdfGzj8HqVNtYwhdkRvuT2YGslXz2J071OebD-Sc4ygsxb5CawxBv8UpHLIqY1ahu2YCb71Q%3D%3D)** You see, Adam Schiff's enablers in the corporate media are already spreading the lie that this race is over. They're saying you and I don't have a chance (just like they did when I entered the race back in October). They're saying that Adam Schiff notched a double victory by advancing to the General Election and drawing me as his opponent. In other words, they're ready, willing and able to cut California voters entirely out of the picture again. My response to Schiff's allies saying they'd rather face me: **_Be careful what you wish for._** I'd liken this to my playing days when a cocky opposing pitcher throws a 94mph fastball right over the plate. I'll tell you, the ball would look as big as a grapefruit before I'd smash it over the fence and touch all the bases on the way home. And look how far we've already made it. I'm in first place in the primary and gaining momentum headed towards the November election. Look, I'm not saying this will be easy. Quite the opposite. It's going to be a nonstop, 58-county fight between now and November 5th. **[That said, I must ask: will you rush a contribution to my senate campaign today?](http://links.rightwaypress.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=e00b9716d4f743d781146f101d6bf1fd&_e=suePF1CEXmlXo39hoovKcNP1x0G5Tr3iWeiWiIiEo9bN11EJOltxGc9adIK4AsLPBfkySgA5D-xwWsS5b2Mf_tvKiMbJYRbIOYYvdEgovfWCakWMMZkiIkaH9Mjme-z1O2_bET9cix8l8ebKp_rnz3KhibJULz634Jd4eZdKRiYjlKt2W2R9uUNX2mInE_JekJV05YlSXNPKUHqzieTkUHy9CS59XXndtX5ShtCJz-ScVRGiFrxNbSqgJkA7uJel5JDxq0M0nxsUL1doKVyHiciDWUHOZ1oJTVCltvyxQi-DbLeZ4aSxooCdPKBv2rsEgLKWOW64ocHWHxDEVI8mU7QptgOs53tgPs4ulTpwtPikYI995yJh608uBkfzNL9LYbUnqtNkk84X4x3vC2-QRg%3D%3D) ** This is going to be an expensive fight. Hiring staff, recruiting and training volunteers, equipping them with the very best technology to identify our voter and secure their vote by November 5th. There's no time to lose. In closing, I can't help but think how Adam Schiff and his team of high-priced DC consultants thought they were being savvy in trying to make sure I became their opponent in General Election. Reports are they even spent money running ads promoting me. But what they've really done is awaken a sleeping giant here. Remember, before it became a wasteland of crime, homelessness, and sky-high taxes, California was a land of dreamers, a land of opportunity. It was a place where a scrawny little kid could start as a bat boy for his heroes, work hard, win a World Series, and land on a Topps baseball card. California can be that place again. America can be that place again. And it starts with throwing out political liars and connivers like Adam Schiff and reclaiming our freedom roots. Time is the most important factor. Thank you!

name: GIFFORDS
subject: Political violence is never the answer
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
We can never, ever accept political violence as normal or excusable in our society.
#

Friends -
I am a survivor of political violence. When I was serving as an Arizona Congresswoman in 2011, a gunman tried to take my life when I was hosting an event for my constituents in front of a Safeway in Tucson.
In 2022, we watched in horror as an assailant broke into the home of Paul and Nancy Pelosi and attacked Paul with a hammer. The intruder entered with the intent to kidnap former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi.
Now, just this past weekend, we saw a gunman try to assassinate former president Donald Trump.
**Political violence is never the answer. President Joe Biden said it best: “We need to resolve our differences at the ballot box, not with bullets.”**
[**If you agree, will you please make a contribution to GIFFORDS PAC to support our work to end political violence?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-july24.-nTEO4&refcode=em240717-1-30&t=1&akid=8515%2E3935704%2EcLv7-G)

name: Katrina
subject: We have a choice to make
body:
| | | | | [](https://katrinaforarizona.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b33bbe17b20417c692e3cf693&id=53d061e5ad&e=a7c9c08fba)
---
| Hello,
The tragic events at the Trump Rally remind us of the all-too-common tragedies we face. We need to collectively strive for a future where our children can experience life - at school, parades, concerts, places of worship, and even political rallies - free from the fear of violence.
Regardless of our background or political party, most of us believe that violence has no place in our political process and weapons of war have no place in our communities. All of us deserve to live our lives and participate in our political process peacefully.
Voters in this election have a choice: to reject a MAGA movement that promotes more violence, or to prioritize a country where we no longer fear for the safety of our loved ones. A country where we ban weapons of war so they’re not used against elementary schoolers or politicians, movie goers or concert attendees. A place where our leaders in Washington honor our freedoms and enact change so we may live without fear of gun violence. For our leaders to honor the votes of the American people and to decide for ourselves what our futures will hold.
I thank you all for your continued support. Let’s move forward, _together_.
---
| Sincerely,Katrina SchaffnerCandidate for US House of Representatives

Time to set the record straight.

| [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/89058961/486049867/1328794144?refcode=ea.ce9a7499-8744-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&ms=ea.ce9a7499-8744-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImNlOWE3NDk5LTg3NDQtZWYxMS04NmMzLTYwNDViZGQ5ZTA5NiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=vvKTOa9KWNvgekn3UOjRO6h1n3CKTsQ_T5WuzKj-GBk=&emci=09ecce27-c043-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&emdi=ce9a7499-8744-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&ceid=4823105)

Let’s talk about some myths surrounding the climate crisis. If you’ve been paying attention to the Republican National Convention this week, you’ve probably heard things like: _“Scientists disagree on the cause of climate change.”_ **False.** _“A couple of degrees of warming is not that big of a deal.”_ **Wrong.** _“The ocean will rise, maybe, and it may go down, also...gives you a little bit more waterfront property if you’re lucky enough to own.”_ **Outrageous.** Here’s the reality: The fossil fuel industry wants you to believe these myths. For decades, they’ve funded efforts to deceive the public about the dangers of burning fossil fuels. Instead of following the science, they orchestrated a massive campaign of denial and deception to protect their profits. They used tactics straight out of the tobacco industry’s playbook, including cherry-picking data, promoting fake experts, and spreading conspiracy theories, all to undermine the scientific consensus and sow doubt. **[We see right through their disinformation tactics, and we need your support to push back and protect our planet. That’s why we set a goal to reach 250 individual donations before the GOP Convention ends tomorrow night, so we can double down on our efforts to combat climate disinformation and elect candidates who aren’t beholden to Big Oil. Can we count on you to chip in?](https://click.everyaction.com/k/89058962/486049868/2105508926?refcode=ea.ce9a7499-8744-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&ms=ea.ce9a7499-8744-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImNlOWE3NDk5LTg3NDQtZWYxMS04NmMzLTYwNDViZGQ5ZTA5NiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=vvKTOa9KWNvgekn3UOjRO6h1n3CKTsQ_T5WuzKj-GBk=)** At the Jane Fonda Climate PAC, we’re not letting the greedy fossil fuel industry get away with this. We are:
* Investing in voter turnout and education to make sure voters have the climate crisis at the top of their minds when they head to the polls this year.

* Exposing Big Oil’s dangerous agenda and holding fossil fuel corporations accountable for their environmental damage.

* Identifying and supporting pro-environment candidates who prioritize solutions to the climate crisis and refuse all money from the fossil fuel lobby and their executives.

* Advocating for clean energy policies that prioritize public health and create green jobs.

President Biden is joining our cause!

I am and always will be a farmer.
| | |

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/89059672/486052285/175992266?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk2950-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODk1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzM2M5ODBhMi04ODQ0LWVmMTEtODZjMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qkAPcwh1JRxZmj-4gp0cDuy44a7TnJ8IRwmFpn08Lj4=)
Can I explain something, folks?
I grew up in a twenty-four-by-thirty-six foot house. I lost three fingers on my left hand in a meat grinding accident when I was a kid. I am and always will be a farmer, like my folks and like my grandparents before me.

**In fact, I’m very proud to be the U.S. Senate’s only working dirt farmer.**
Every spring, I spend a lot of weeks working the stubble, getting equipment ready for planting, and out in the field seeding. Come summer, I am out there harvesting. I maintain my own heavy equipment and deliver my grain in a truck that’s a bit bigger than what any of my colleagues drive.

I buy grease by the case and seeds by the ton. I butcher my own beef. My wife, Sharla, and I work the farm hand-in-hand.
The task of scheduling my work in the Senate around the inflexible timing of farm responsibilities drives my staff crazy — but they know my farm work is non-negotiable. It keeps me, quite literally, grounded.

**And rather than spend my days hobnobbing with special interests, I rely on hardworking folks like you to power everything we do.**
**[That’s why I’m personally asking you to join my reelection team and split $5 between Jeanne Shaheen and my campaign today to help us defend Montana’s Senate seat. Anything you can give makes a difference.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/89059673/486052286/175992266?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=jtk2950-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODk1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzM2M5ODBhMi04ODQ0LWVmMTEtODZjMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qkAPcwh1JRxZmj-4gp0cDuy44a7TnJ8IRwmFpn08Lj4=)** | | [Contribute](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/89059674/486052287/175992266?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk2950-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODk1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzM2M5ODBhMi04ODQ0LWVmMTEtODZjMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qkAPcwh1JRxZmj-4gp0cDuy44a7TnJ8IRwmFpn08Lj4=)

Friend, activists have spent 100 years fighting to add the Equal Rights Amendment to our Constitution. This long-overdue amendment would establish that our civil rights cannot be infringed upon or taken away on the basis of gender.
Now that the Supreme Court has overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , far-right legislators have unleashed a slew of attacks against our reproductive rights and our right to privacy. **Passing the ERA is our best bet to restore those crucial rights — and we can't wait a moment longer.**
Polling shows 85% of voters support the ERA — and 38 states have ratified it, clearing the way to add it to the Constitution. But an arbitrary deadline is stopping us from finally certifying this amendment!
**Thankfully, Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand has introduced a resolution that would allow us to ignore this deadline and make the ERA the law of the land.** With bipartisan support, filibuster reform and strong grassroots backing, Kirsten can get the job done.
